title: Who shot down T1-323
reading: Barber's run from astern brings T1-323 down; official credit stays shared
basis: Both attacks are flown as reported; the bomber falls after Barber's run, as Pacific Wrecks and Haulman conclude, while the Air Force's shared credit stands.

title: Where Hine was last seen
reading: Hit four miles north of Shortland at 09:41:36; last seen south of it at 09:45:40
basis: The same-day report and Holmes, Hine's element leader (MACR 609), last see him south of Shortland; Mitchell, from top cover, sees him smoking north of it with Zeros making passes, which the replay takes as the moment he is hit. Wilson Strait, between Vella Lavella and Ranongga (OpenStreetMap), lies south-east, on the way home, not south-west as Pacific Wrecks has it. South of Shortland lies about 40 km from the fight off Moila Point, a few minutes beyond MACR 609's 9:40. He keeps his height over the island's hills and loses it beyond.

records.says: During these minutes, Hines' left engine started to smoke and he was last seen losing altitude south of Shortland Island.
records.label: typescript, read from the scan

records.says: MACR 599 states Hine was last seen by Major Mitchell four miles north of Shortland just above the sea with one engine smoking and three Zeros making firing passes.

MACR 609 states Hine was last seen south of Shortland at 9:40am by Lt. Besby T. Holmes, seen trailing smoke or vapor from the left engine and headed in the direction of Wilson Strait to the southwest of Shortland.
No trace of his plane was ever found and he was never seen to crash.
